provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.diagnosis: The run did not fail on any visible-grid mismatch. The fixture variants and the 32 fresh base inputs that were sampled produced no reported solver error. The run stopped at the sampling stage with 'TimeoutError: reference/generator deadline', and 51 seeds were rejected. The cause is the constructor's random branch. It first fixes num_boxes uniformly in [4,12] and the box sizes. Then it re-draws all positions jointly in an unbounded `while True` loop until common.overlaps(..., 1) reports no padded overlap. The padded footprint of 8 to 12 boxes of size 2..7 (one up to 13 wide) is often close to or above the free area of an 18-19 square grid. For those draws, the chance that a joint random placement is non-overlapping is astronomically small or zero, so the loop never ends. Nothing is wrong with the ray mechanism, the D4 handling, or the palette handling in the factory. The factory is resubmitted unchanged in substance.
draft_notes.constructor_issue: The constructor's sampler is unbounded. It rejection-samples all box positions jointly, with no attempt limit, after committing to num_boxes and the sizes. High box counts make it effectively non-terminating, so the host hits its generator deadline. This is a sampling defect only. The canonical fixtures, their labels and the rule are consistent: rays from each side of the 8 rectangle paint 0/2 cells as 4 and stop at the first 1 cell or the border. I found no fixture contradiction, no indexing bug and no hidden tie-break. The proposed repair places boxes one after another with a bounded number of tries per box and a bounded number of whole-scene restarts. On each restart it re-draws num_boxes and the sizes. After placement it still requires common.overlaps(..., 1) to be false and still requires that colours 1, 2 and 8 all appear. The explicit validate() fixtures are untouched. Expected distribution change: (a) sequential placement is not exactly the joint-uniform distribution conditioned on non-overlap. (b) Box counts or sizes that are infeasible or extremely rare to place are resampled, so very crowded 11-12 box scenes appear less often than the nominal uniform count draw. The original sampler could only produce such scenes by running for an unbounded time. (c) The long box (index -1) is placed first so it has room. This does not change list semantics, because colour 8 stays at index 0 and the boxes are disjoint. The scenes are not ambiguous: the output is a deterministic function of the visible input, so no uniqueness filter is needed.
draft_notes.explanation: Mechanism: find the single solid anchor rectangle (palette[8]). From every cell on each of its four sides, cast a one-cell-wide ray straight outward. The ray paints palette[4] over background and red (palette[0] and palette[2]). It stops at the first blocker cell (palette[1]) or at the grid border. This set of four rays is closed under D4, so in visible coordinates the program is the same for every d4. Up/down rays still cover the visible rectangle's columns and left/right rays its rows, and only the colour constants are specialised. The host failure was a generator timeout during sampling, not a solver mismatch. The proposed constructor repair replaces the unbounded joint rejection loop with bounded sequential placement. It keeps the size ranges, the count range, the long box, the 1-cell separation verified by common.overlaps, the colour requirements, the output rendering and every explicit fixture.
draft_notes.limitations: Bounded sequential placement changes layout sampling relative to joint rejection. The requested object count is retained, dimensions are conditioned on fitting, and exhaustion raises rather than reducing count. No claim is made about an exactly uniform distribution over placements.
draft_notes.host_sampler_revision: Retain the drawn 4..12 object count across all placement retries; place larger sampled boxes first; resample dimensions/layouts only. Exhaustion raises. Original fixtures verified byte-equivalent as Python structures. Fresh audit pending.
draft_notes.proposal_limitations_before_host_change: The factory assumes exactly one anchor-coloured solid rectangle, which matches the constructor's domain. If several anchors were present, it would use their joint bounding box. The repaired sampler changes the fresh-scene distribution slightly. Placement is sequential rather than joint-uniform, and crowded high-count draws that cannot be placed are resampled, so 11-12 box scenes are under-represented compared with the nominal uniform count draw. In theory the sampler can raise RuntimeError after 2000 failed restarts, but low box counts almost always place on the first try, so this should not occur in practice. I have not run any tests; the constructor and factory both need host review and execution.
draft_notes.host_review: Canonical fixtures unchanged; requested counts 4, 8, 12 checked explicitly with non-overlap and all required colours. Fresh audit: 1,000 unique base inputs, 8,000 augmented checks, 16 fixture variants, 7.22 seconds, zero sampler rejections. Solver casts rays in visible coordinates, with blocker colour 1 and traversable colours 0/2; no query-answer or latent-layout access.
